judgments.title: Core logic test suite (ErgController, registry, settings, classifier, adapter contracts)
required_evidence: Gradle jvmTest passes: ErgController engages ERG at remembered wattage with 120 W first-use default; 3 W step math and direct-entry commit semantics; 50-600 W clamping including boundary entries 49/50/600/601; rapid adjustments coalesce to one in-flight write; reconnect state machine reapplies target when riding and stays paused when paused; pause persists across restart via persisted state; Resume reapplies saved target; device registry reports capabilities from GATT inventory; metric-source map resolves all metrics to the trainer; settings store round-trips trainer identity, wattage, paused flag; ProtocolClassifier labels the committed Hammer fixture controllable with constants matching the fixture; BLE adapter contract tests against the fake Blue Falcon wrapper

judgments.title: Hardware capture provenance and classifier finalization

criteria: R1 Discovery: the evidence shows the powered-on Hammer was found by a live BlueZ scan on the target Linux machine, listed by advertised name without a hard-coded address.

R2 Capture provenance: the committed fixture (core/src/commonTest/resources/fixtures/hammer-gatt-inventory.json) carries capture provenance (date, method, machine) in the implementation notes or fixture itself, and its service/characteristic list is consistent with real hardware capture, not a hand-invented FTMS template.

R3 Classifier finalization: ProtocolClassifier constants match the captured fixture; the fixture's control path (FTMS 0x1826/0x2AD9 or the CycleOps proprietary service actually observed) is reflected in the committed constants, and no placeholder markers remain.
R4 Minimum-load evidence: the capture notes state what lowest-load command the trainer accepted (or explicitly record that none exists), since Pause and safe-disconnect depend on it.
R5 Privacy: the committed fixture and evidence contain no Bluetooth addresses (probe privacy scan reports clean).

required_evidence: probe output: fixture present, parseable, and service list printed
probe output: classifier constants with no placeholder markers

judgments.title: 5-minute smoke ride on the physical Hammer

criteria: R1 Connect and ERG: the ride evidence shows the app connected to the real Hammer from the devices screen and ERG engaged automatically at the remembered wattage (120 W on a fresh profile) without any enable action.
R2 Live telemetry: actual power and speed were live on the ride screen for the duration; the evidence shows target vs actual displayed separately.
R3 Adjustment: ±3 W buttons, ↑/↓ keys, and direct entry each changed the load during the ride, with the trainer physically responding; out-of-range entries clamped with a visible notice.
R4 Interruption recovery: a deliberate Bluetooth interruption mid-ride recovered automatically and reapplied the riding target; an interruption while paused recovered into the paused state.
R5 Pause/Resume: Pause dropped the trainer to its lowest supported load with telemetry still live; Resume reapplied the target.
R6 Staleness: the evidence shows (log or screen capture) readings displaying '—' within 3 seconds of telemetry loss, with a visible recovery attempt in the status line.
R7 Safe disconnect: disconnect requested minimum load before releasing; the evidence confirms the trainer released resistance, or shows the unconfirmed-release state honestly when it could not.

R8 Evidence quality: the ride evidence (log excerpt and/or screen capture) is committed under docs/features/002-desktop-ble-erg-mvp/implementation/, is at least 5 minutes of riding, contains no Bluetooth addresses, and reflects the real Hammer (not the fake client).

required_evidence: probe output: implementation evidence files listed and non-empty
committed ride evidence: log excerpt or screen capture of the full checklist ride
rider confirmation of each checklist item in the evidence doc
